text: After the after-action report, Dana Whitfield asks the question the slide deck didn't answer: how do we know there isn't a similar blind spot somewhere else in the platform right now? Casey Lindqvist follows with the second hard one — why didn't load-testing catch this before the sale?

The load-test answer is precise: the pre-sale test ran against a fixed-size node pool with no cluster-autoscaler activity. Production's real autoscaling event, adding nodes mid-sale with no availability-zone awareness in the scheduler, simply had no equivalent moment in the test.

A credible answer to Dana's question has three parts: the exact bug is fixed and proven under a repeat load test, the same dashboard that missed it now has a per-AZ panel that makes a future imbalance impossible to miss, and a specific audit of every other cluster-wide average metric in the platform is now a named, scoped next step.

Guessing that this was the only blind spot would have closed the meeting cleanly, but it would have been confidence dressed up over an actual unknown. Naming the fix, the new visibility, and the planned audit is what makes 'we're on it' credible instead of hollow.
